newsitem.title: USA: Praxair to raise U.S. prices May 1.
newsitem.headline: Praxair to raise U.S. prices May 1.

text.p: Praxair Inc said Wednesday it will raise prices for carbon dioxide and hydrogen delivered to customers in the United States effective May 1.
The price increases will average 4 percent for carbon dioxide and 7 percent for hydrogen, it said.
It said that individual price adjustments will vary, depending on local supply conditions, contract terms, and regional variations in production and distribution costs.

Paul Bilek, president of the company's North American industrial gases unit, said the company was experiencing rising raw gas costs and tight supply for carbon dioxide, and a much higher rate of government and commercial consumption of hydrogen.
"Consequently, to meet customer demands, Praxair faces much higher costs for energy and transportation," he said.
Praxair said it was also notifying its liquid oxygen, nitrogen, argon and helium customers that it will be reducing or eliminating price discounts, consistent with contract terms and conditions.
"Praxair continues to work on productivity programs to constrain those costs under our control and to minimize the impact on customers," Bilek said.
He said the programs include the addition of new capacity, plant modernization and the commercialization of cost effective on-site supply systems.
Praxair is the largest industrial gases supplier in North and South America, and one of the largest worldwide, with annual sales of $4.4 billion.
